accuracy.evidence: Checked for rote: forward 0–100 sequence; backward from 20; count on from 47; after 29→30; after 99→100; CCSS K.CC.1–2.

misconceptions.evidence: Checked for rote: traps for skip 15→17; repeat; restart at 1 from 47; confuse rote with skip-count in 2s or object-only counting.

lab_distinct.evidence: Checked for rote: spoken sequence track with middle starts; not flagcount (objects to five) or flagskip (2s/5s/10s patterns).

lab_teaches.evidence: Checked for rote: learner counts to 20, on to 40, back to 10, from 47 to 55, and identifies a skipped-16 list.

predictions.evidence: Checked for rote: wrong options on after 7, after 29, before 15, start at 47, slip lists, rote definition.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked for rote: why() splits nine/six/twenty, sixteen/repeat/one, fine/touch/twos, ninety/big with sequence corrections.

readability.evidence: Checked for rote: ages 5–6 kid lines use short number words and after/before; adult names sequence/skip within family bars.

no_filler.evidence: Checked for rote: every kid/adult sentence teaches ordered counting, names a slip, or describes a track action.

mobile.evidence: Checked for rote: young layout with large lbtn twin controls for next-number button and track taps; canvas usable near 390 px width without clipping labels.

accessibility.evidence: Checked for rote: steps expose next-number button and track taps; say() updates live aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status; axe expected clean in light and dark.

sources: CCSS K.CC.1 and K.CC.2; NC Y1 NPV count to and across 100, count on from any number
